sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Auburn, WA?
sections.html:
Auburn is a King County city of 86,301 people (Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025) with a small piece that crosses into Pierce County, so the county that bills your property tax depends on which side of the line the house sits. Auburn leans toward ownership: 60.6% of housing is owner-occupied, the median value of an owner-occupied home was $547,900 for 2020 to 2024, and the typical household has 2.79 people. Median household income was $97,884 and the average commute was 30.5 minutes.

The city lost a little population after 2020, from 87,256 at the census to the 2025 estimate, even though it had grown from 70,180 in 2010. A good share of that earlier jump came from annexation. In 2008 Auburn annexed the West Hill and Lea Hill areas of unincorporated King County, which added about 15,000 residents, and on January 1, 2024 it took in the 155-acre Bridges neighborhood from Kent.

That history explains why an "Auburn" mailing address does not always mean the City of Auburn. Some addresses that include Auburn belong to King County, Kent or Federal Way, and the city's permit page asks you to check its interactive map before assuming city rules apply to your property.

sections.h2: How did Auburn grow, and which neighborhoods do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The town was platted in 1886 as Slaughter, named for an officer killed in 1855, and incorporated on June 13, 1891. The legislature changed the name to Auburn on February 21, 1893, after Auburn, New York, where residents shared a hops-farming economy. Floods on the White and Green rivers shaped the early valley until Mud Mountain Dam and Howard A. Hanson Dam were completed, which let the city grow without that constraint.

The largest recent build-out was Lakeland Hills. Construction began in 1985 on a master-planned community in the hills southeast of downtown, and by 2007 it had 3,600 homes and about 6,000 residents. Auburn voted in 1997 to annex part of it, and the city finished taking in the Pierce County portion by the end of that decade.

  • Downtown: historic buildings, a traditional main street and Craftsman-style houses from the 1920s.
  • Lea Hill: mostly residential, east of the valley, and home to Green River College.
  • Lakeland Hills: master-planned and split between King and Pierce counties.
  • Terminal Park: middle-class housing near the rail yard, named for railroad workers.
  • Forest Villa: residential, around Game Farm Park.
  • West Hill: borders Federal Way.
  • Hidden Valley: planned development east of Lakeland Hills overlooking North Lake Tapps.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Auburn homes?
sections.html:
Most of the city is in the Auburn School District, which is larger than the city itself and also serves Algona, Pacific and some unincorporated areas. Parts of north Auburn are served by the Federal Way and Kent school districts, and the Pierce County portion falls in the Dieringer School District. Because the boundary depends on the street, confirm the district for your exact address before you list.

The public high schools are Auburn High School, Auburn Mountainview High School and Auburn Riverside High School. Private options include Auburn Adventist Academy, Rainier Christian High School, Valley Christian School and Holy Family School, and Green River College is on Lea Hill. The Auburn School District, with 2,536 employees, is the city's second largest employer.

sections.h2: How do jobs, roads and weather affect Auburn houses?
sections.html:
Auburn's economy leans on aerospace, distribution and health care. The Boeing plant, opened in 1966, is the city's largest employer with about 3,600 workers, followed by the school district, Muckleshoot Tribal Enterprises (1,472), MultiCare Auburn Medical Center (1,208), Green River College (857) and a Safeway distribution center (800). Those headcounts are from the city's 2022 annual financial report.

For commuters, State Route 167 (the Valley Freeway) and State Route 18 run through town. Auburn station is a hub for the Green River Valley: Sounder trains reach downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes, Sound Transit buses connect to Federal Way, Sumner and Kent, and King County Metro buses serve Auburn Way and Green River College.

The climate is mild and wet. Average precipitation is 37.1 inches a year, with the heaviest months being November (6.1 inches), December (5.8) and January (5.3). Summers are dry, with July and August highs near 77 and 78 degrees, and the record high is 100.

sections.h2: Do I need a rental license in Auburn?
sections.html:
Yes for most rentals. Auburn requires an owner to obtain a Rental Housing License for most forms of renting residential property, and the program exists so the city has current ownership and management information for non-owner-occupied homes. If you are selling a house that tenants occupy, confirm your license is current before you list. The city lists the following arrangements.

Rental typeCity requirement
Owner-occupied home, renting rooms to 2 or fewer peopleCity business license not required; occupancy limit is family plus 2.
Owner-occupied home, renting rooms to more than 2 peopleCity business license required; occupancy limit is family plus 4.
Non-owner-occupied home, one lease for the entire homeCity business license required; no inspection.
Non-owner-occupied home, more than one lease (communal residence)License required; occupancy limit of 4; initial inspection before issuance and annual inspection before renewal.
ApartmentsCity business license required; no inspection.

Source: City of Auburn Rental Housing. Rental license rules are in Auburn City Code 5.22, and the Permit Center answers questions at 253-931-3090, option 2.

sections.h2: What permits and disclosures come up when selling an Auburn house?
sections.html:
Auburn takes permit applications electronically through MyBuildingPermit.com. Electrical permits inside city limits come from the Washington Department of Labor and Industries, and a house on a septic system needs approval from the King County or Pierce County health department for most changes. If you built a deck, finished a basement or changed wiring, find out now whether a permit exists, because buyers and inspectors ask.

State law also puts a form in your hands. Under RCW 64.06.020, the seller of improved residential property delivers a completed disclosure statement, unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt, no later than five business days after mutual acceptance of a written contract. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind. The form asks about title, water, sewer, structural conditions and more, so start gathering records before you list.

sections.h2: How are property tax and transfer tax handled when selling in Auburn?
sections.html:
A King County parcel is billed by the King County treasurer and a Pierce County parcel by the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer, whose office can be reached at (253) 798-6111. Under RCW 84.56.020, the first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Taxes are a lien from January 1, and RCW 84.60.020 splits the year between seller and buyer by days when the contract is silent. Escrow normally prorates the bill at closing.

The seller usually pays the state real estate excise tax, due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the first $551,000 of price is taxed at 1.1%, with 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000 and higher rates above that. Auburn's Census median value of $547,900 sits just below the first bracket, so a typical sale there would be taxed entirely at the lowest state rate, plus the local share. Ask your closing agent to confirm the local rate and any exemption you may claim.

Washington lets residents 61 or older, certain disabled owners and some veterans claim a property tax exemption under RCW 84.36.381, and the status can move to a replacement home if you sell.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to if I live in Auburn?
faqs.a: Most Auburn parcels are in King County and are billed by the King County treasurer. Homes in the Pierce County portion, including part of Lakeland Hills, are billed by the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer.

faqs.q: Does my Auburn mailing address mean I am inside Auburn city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Some addresses that include Auburn fall under King County, Kent or Federal Way, so use the city's interactive map before assuming city permit and rental rules apply.

faqs.q: Do I need a city license to rent rooms in my Auburn home?
faqs.a: You need a City of Auburn business license if you rent rooms to more than two people. Renting to two or fewer people in an owner-occupied home does not require one, and the occupancy limit is family plus 2.

faqs.q: How soon must I give the buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Deliver it no later than five business days after the buyer and seller mutually accept a written contract, unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: What state transfer tax rate would apply to a typical Auburn sale?
faqs.a: For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state rate is 1.1% on the portion of the price up to $551,000, so a sale at Auburn's $547,900 median value would fall in that bracket. A local rate is added.
